prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one ORIGINAL MASTER painting for one Bhagavad Gita verse in a Sanskrit reader. Generate a single square 1:1 image, 2048x2048 or the highest actually supported native square resolution. Consistent series style: refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, subtle ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting, quiet atmospheric daylight. The image must illustrate THIS VERSE'S ACTUAL MEANING. Read the exact source meaning below; derive a concrete, intelligible scene or a restrained symbolic interpretation of that teaching. Never simply paint an unrelated chariot, generic temple or anonymous landscape. Compose one coherent scene, no collage or infographic. Keep important faces, hands, relationships and narrative objects inside the central 60% of width and central 50% of height, surrounded by ample low-detail sky, ground and paper atmosphere. No important subject cut by an edge. This one master must support portrait/landscape phones and tablets through safe proportional fitting. No text of any kind, no verse number, no letters, no Sanskrit/Roman typography, no watermark, no frame, no UI. Text will be rendered separately by the app over the image at a user-adjustable default image opacity of 48%. If Krishna is depicted, maintain a youthful calm blue-skinned figure in muted golden-yellow garments, a restrained peacock-feather crown, no modern jewelry. Arjuna is a dark-haired warrior with a small crown, bow and understated bronze armor. Use them only when the meaning warrants them; the scene or analogy remains verse-specific.  Reference (DO NOT DRAW THIS TEXT): Bhagavad Gītā 8.8. Exact Sanskrit: अभ्यासयोगयुक्तेन चेतसा नान्यगामिना। परमं पुरुषं दिव्यं याति पार्थानुचिन्तयन्॥ Exact stored meaning: O Pārtha, one who meditates continuously with a mind made steadfast through the yoga of practice (abhyāsa-yoga), not wandering to anything else — that person reaches the Supreme Divine Puruṣa. Chapter context: The imperishable, remembrance, transition, cosmic cycles and paths. Use symbolic contemplative imagery without depicting bodily distress, corpses or literal metaphysical claims as historical events. Previous verse context only, do not substitute for the target: Therefore, at all times remember Me and fight. With mind and intellect surrendered to Me (mayy arpita-mano-buddhiḥ), you shall come to Me alone — without doubt. Next verse context only, do not substitute for the target: Whoever meditates on the Seer (kavi), the Ancient (purāṇa), the Ruler (anuśāsitāram), subtler than the atom (aṇor aṇīyāṃsam), the Sustainer of all (sarvasya dhātāram), of inconceivable form (acintya-rūpam), luminous as the sun (āditya-varṇam), beyond all darkness — Final instruction: center the distinctive content of the TARGET meaning, not the neighboring verses. No fabricated teaching or unrelated religious scene.
